        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 123af9043e93cb6f235207d260d50f832cdb5439 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2018 11:08:38 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: au1x: Fix timeout tests in au1xac97c_ac97_read()

The loop timeout doesn't work because it's a post op and ends with "tmo"
set to -1.  I changed it from a post-op to a pre-op and I changed the
initial the starting value from 5 to 6 so we still iterate 5 times.  I
left the other as it was because it's a large number.

Fixes: b3c70c9ea62a ("ASoC: Alchemy AC97C/I2SC audio support")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
---
 sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c | 6 +++---
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c b/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c
index 29a97d52e8ad..66d6c52e7761 100644
--- a/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c
+++ b/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c
@@ -91,8 +91,8 @@ static unsigned short au1xac97c_ac97_read(struct snd_ac97 *ac97,
 	do {
 		mutex_lock(&ctx->lock);
 
-		tmo = 5;
-		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && tmo--)
+		tmo = 6;
+		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && --tmo)
 			udelay(21);	/* wait an ac97 frame time */
 		if (!tmo) {
 			pr_debug("ac97rd timeout #1\n");
@@ -105,7 +105,7 @@ static unsigned short au1xac97c_ac97_read(struct snd_ac97 *ac97,
 		 * poll, Forrest, poll...
 		 */
 		tmo = 0x10000;
-		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && tmo--)
+		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && --tmo)
 			asm volatile ("nop");
 		data = RD(ctx, AC97_CMDRESP);
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The loop for checking the timeout condition in the function `au1xac97c_ac97_read()` did not properly decrement the timeout counter (`tmo`) before checking its value, resulting in an infinite loop if the condition `RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP` remained true. The issue was that `tmo` was being set to -1 after the loop ended due to a post-decrement operation, which led to incorrect timeout handling. The patch fixes this by changing the decrement to be a pre-decrement operation, ensuring that the timeout checks function correctly.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>

    <textN>

Root cause:
The loop for checking the timeout condition in the function `au1xac97c_ac97_read()` did not properly decrement the timeout counter (`tmo`) before checking its value, resulting in an infinite loop if the condition `RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP` remained true. The issue was that `tmo` was being set to -1 after the loop ended due to a post-decrement operation, which led to incorrect timeout handling. The patch fixes this by changing the decrement to be a pre-decrement operation, ensuring that the timeout checks function correctly.
